method: Reuse the existing ShotPoisson method: train attack/defence on half actual goals plus half prior shots on target multiplied by a goals-per-shot scale fitted exclusively on prior league games. Blend the resulting Poisson probabilities with fixed Elo. This is a shot proxy, not xG.
informationFence: Every historical forecast excludes results and statistics on or after the day immediately preceding kickoff; the shot scale, attack/defence, goal-only reference and Elo all obey that same conservative date fence.
missingShotPolicy: Retain every verified result. If either club's shots on target are missing or invalid, train that fixture using its actual goals without substituting zero shots. Report coverage and fallback counts.
sourcePolicy: Use the exact E1 CSV bytes pinned by the previous study, verify every raw SHA-256, enforce E1, and match all normalized identities and scores against the frozen 6252-result archive. Persist a new normalized shots snapshot for offline reproduction. No odds or target-match statistics are predictors.
pointGate: Both metrics improve over the same-recipe goal-only model and v1 in every reported period, on identical fixtures.
historicalGate: Point gate plus both audit calendar-day paired bootstrap upper bounds below zero against both the goal-only model and v1.
limitations: All historical periods were inspected in the preceding ELC experiment. This is further retrospective development, not an untouched test or proof of future accuracy.
Only one fixed shot recipe is evaluated; neither its mixture weight nor decay is retuned after inspecting later results.
Shots on target do not identify shot location or chance quality and must not be presented as measured xG.
CSV publication times are unavailable, so the immediately preceding calendar day is excluded conservatively.
Same-division history can be sparse for promoted or relegated clubs; the common v1 eligibility rule and all excluded counts remain visible.
The archive contains missing and inconsistent statistics. Such fixtures retain verified goals and are never removed to improve measured accuracy.
Player availability, lineups, weather and betting odds are not numeric inputs in this experiment.
The original one-hundred-match series, public model and goal-only study remain unchanged. Any prospective comparison requires its own actual registration before kickoff.
